data.text: What you build

One real explainer video, built start to finish with Claude Code and HyperFrames: a brief, a fact-checked script, a storyboard you review before anything moves, illustrations in one locked style, a synced voice and a review loop. Every command and prompt from the video is below, in order.
Starter repo (everything from the video)
Commands with <slug> mean the video folder Claude created under videos/. List them with: ls videos
1 Set up
Windows: install Node.js (22 or newer)
macOS: install Node.js (22 or newer)
Windows: install ffmpeg
macOS: install ffmpeg
Windows (PowerShell): install Claude Code
data.richText:
Official installer from the Claude Code docs. Open a new terminal afterwards.

Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise or Console account. The free claude.ai plan does not include it.

Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/setup

data.text: macOS / Linux / WSL: install Claude Code
data.richText: Official installer from the Claude Code docs. Open a new terminal afterwards.

data.text: Python 3.8+ (for the ElevenLabs voice script)
data.richText:
Windows: winget install Python.Python.3.12

macOS: brew install python

data.text: Check your machine
data.richText: whisper-cpp shows as optional: you only need it for the free voice route.

data.text: Install the official HyperFrames skills for Claude Code
data.richText: They install into your user folder, so every project sees them.

data.text: Clone the starter
Install (pins one HyperFrames version for the repo)
Pick a voice in the ElevenLabs voice library and copy its voice ID
data.richText: The explainer in the video uses the stock voice Sarah: EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL

data.text: Create an ElevenLabs API key
data.richText: The key is a secret. It goes into .env, never into a prompt or a screenshot.

data.text: Copy the example env file and paste in your key and voice ID
data.richText: .env is already in .gitignore. The free ElevenLabs plan is non-commercial only; a monetized channel needs a paid plan (ElevenLabs on publishing).

data.text: Connect the Higgsfield MCP server (needs a paid Higgsfield plan)

codeBlock.code: claude mcp add --transport http higgsfield https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp

data.richText:
Or add https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp as a connector on claude.ai (Settings, Connectors).

Higgsfield: what is the MCP

data.text: Start Claude Code in the repo folder
Log in to Higgsfield once: run /mcp and pick higgsfield
2 The brief
Type into Claude Code (swap in your topic, take, sources and look)

codeBlock.code:
/hyperframes Make a 2-minute explainer about prompt caching for developers who use Claude Code.
Use the standard explainer pipeline. Collaborative: show me the storyboard before you build.
My take: most of your Claude Code bill is Claude re-reading the same context, and caching is the
kitchen where the prep is already done. The idea scenes use that kitchen as illustrations; the
numbers stay diagrams.
Sources: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching and
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching
Look: cream paper #F4F1EA, charcoal ink #1A1815, one clay accent #C15F3C. Playfair Display
headlines, Inter body, JetBrains Mono labels.
Voice: ElevenLabs. No music. YouTube, 16:9.

data.richText: "Use the standard explainer pipeline" routes it to /faceless-explainer. It recommends an angle, may offer a few additions, and asks what's missing.

data.text: Answer its questions in a line each (the tutorial's answers)

codeBlock.code:
1. Yes, the narrative concept.
2. Both. Keep one kitchen across the idea scenes: empty, prepped, serving.
3. No, only the two docs pages.

data.richText: The answers land in BRIEF.md.

data.text: 3 The script
Read fact-check.md: one row per claim, with the sentence from the source it rests on
data.richText: In the tutorial run it dropped two claims the docs didn't support and marked the take as an opinion.

data.text: No fact-check.md in your run? Ask for it

codeBlock.code:
Check every number in SCRIPT.md against the sources and write fact-check.md with one row per
claim: value, source URL, verified or wrong. Fix any wrong ones in the script.

data.text: CLAUDE.md makes Claude write the narration for the ear
data.richText: Commas or full stops instead of dashes, file names written the way they're said (CLAUDE.md becomes "Claude dot M D"). The voice reads exactly what's on the page.

data.text: 4 The design system
Check frame.md once: the preset the workflow picked, remixed onto your colours and fonts
data.richText: Every frame inherits it. Fix anything that is off now, before the storyboard is drawn on it.

data.text: Confirm it and let Claude draw the sketches

codeBlock.code: The frames look right. Draw the sketches.

data.text: 5 The storyboard review
Open the sketch sheet in your browser
data.richText: Every frame as a static sketch, in the real fonts, colours and text. Nothing moves yet.

data.text: Ask for changes frame by frame (the tutorial's change)

codeBlock.code: Frame 11 has too much text on screen. Cut it to the /usage card and let the voice say the two habits. Show me the sheet again.

data.text: Confirm when it looks right
data.richText: CLAUDE.md tells Claude never to build before you confirm the sheet.

data.text: 6 Art direction
Claude runs /art-direction for the metaphor scenes and shows you the first plate
data.richText: One prompt per scene with a locked style block, the first kept plate as a reference for the rest, a checklist for redoing plates, and a ledger of every prompt in assets/art/. Every image costs Higgsfield credits.

data.text: If it doesn't start on its own
Put a fix into the style lock so every later plate gets it (the tutorial's redo)

codeBlock.code: Redo it. Add full-bleed, no plate border to the style lock so plates B and C get it too.

data.text: Keep the plate and let it make the rest

codeBlock.code: Keep it. Go on with B and C.

data.text: 7 The voice
The workflow makes the narration with the ElevenLabs voice from .env
data.richText: Writes narration.wav and transcript.json: the start time of every word.

data.text: Free route instead: Kokoro voice + word timings

codeBlock.code:
npx hyperframes tts videos/<slug>/script.txt --voice af_heart -o videos/<slug>/narration.wav
npx hyperframes transcribe videos/<slug>/narration.wav -d videos/<slug>

data.richText: Word timings need whisper.cpp: brew install whisper-cpp on macOS; on Windows download whisper-bin-x64.zip from the whisper.cpp releases and point HYPERFRAMES_WHISPER_PATH at whisper-cli.exe.

data.text: 8 The build
Approve the plates and start the build

codeBlock.code: They look right. Start the build.

data.richText: One sub-agent per frame, then Claude assembles the video and runs the checks.

data.text: Run the checks
Watch it in the studio
Render it
data.richText: If Claude's own render can't start Chrome from its shell, run this command yourself.

data.text: 9 The review loop
Let Claude review its own frames
data.richText: A grid of 18 stills, scores out of 10 and the three worst problems with timestamps. Don't chase the scores; fix the timestamped problems.

data.text: Apply the fixes
Render again, then run /review again
data.richText: Stop when the list gets shorter and the problems get smaller. If npx hyperframes check still fails after a fix, believe the check: pull a full-size frame from the render and look.
